Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB        Document 53      Filed 06/22/26   Page 1 of 9




                                   1
                                   2
                                   3
                                   4
                                   5                        IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                                   6                    FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA
                                   7
                                   8     BAYERISCHE MOTOREN WERKE                      Case No. 26-cv-05274-CRB
                                         AG,
                                   9
                                                      Plaintiff,                       ORDER GRANTING MOTION FOR
                                  10                                                   PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION
                                                v.
                                  11
                                         ZYNC INC.,
                                  12
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                                      Defendant.
                                  13
                                             Bayerische Motoren Werke Aktiengesellschaft (“BMW”) sues to enforce a forum
                                  14
                                       selection clause against Zync Inc. (“Zync”). Compl. (dkt. 1). Zync and BMW of North
                                  15
                                       America, LLC (“BMW NA”), BMW’s subsidiary, initially entered into a Pilot Project
                                  16
                                       Agreement (“PPA”) for in-vehicle infotainment technology. Id. ¶ 18. That agreement was
                                  17
                                       subject to the terms of BMW’s and Zync’s prior confidentiality agreement (“NDA”),
                                  18
                                       which contained a forum selection clause and choice-of-law provision. Id. ¶ 21. Those
                                  19
                                       terms state that the agreement “shall be governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of
                                  20
                                       Germany and the exclusive place of jurisdiction shall be Munich, unless a different place
                                  21
                                       of jurisdiction is required by mandatory law.” Id.
                                  22
                                             Eventually, the partnership soured and Zync sued BMW NA in state court on April
                                  23
                                       14, 2025, claiming that BMW NA misappropriated its trade secrets. Compl. ¶ 25. BMW
                                  24
                                       NA moved to dismiss the action based on the NDA’s forum selection clause. Id. ¶ 26.
                                  25
                                       Before the state court reached a decision on BMW NA’s motion to dismiss, Zync filed a
                                  26
                                       complaint against BMW and BMW NA with the International Trade Commission (“ITC”)
                                  27
                                       on February 23, 2026, premised on the same theory as the state action. Id. ¶ 28. On May
                                  28
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB           Document 53       Filed 06/22/26    Page 2 of 9




                                   1   12, 2026, the state court granted BMW NA’s motion and dismissed the case on forum
                                   2   selection grounds. Id. ¶ 29.
                                   3           BMW moved for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction enjoining
                                   4   Zync from participating in the ITC action to halt the process before the Court can resolve
                                   5   BMW’s anti-injunction motion. Mot. (dkt. 10). Zync opposed. Opp’n (dkt. 19). This
                                   6   Court granted BMW’s motion for a temporary restraining order on June 12, 2026. Dkt. 29.
                                   7   The ITC proceedings are currently stayed pending the resolution of BMW’s motion for a
                                   8   preliminary injunction. Dkt. 34. The parties both filed additional briefs following the
                                   9   temporary restraining order. Reply (dkt. 41); Sur-reply (dkt. 40); Second Reply (dkt. 44-
                                  10   2). The Court GRANTS BMW’s motion.
                                  11   I.      LEGAL STANDARD
                                  12           A party seeking a preliminary injunction must establish: (1) a likelihood of success
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   on the merits; (2) a likelihood of irreparable harm absent preliminary relief; (3) that the
                                  14   balance of equities tips in the plaintiff’s favor; and (4) that an injunction is in the public
                                  15   interest. Winter v. Nat. Res. Def. Council, Inc., 555 U.S. 7, 20 (2008). The “[l]ikelihood
                                  16   of success on the merits ‘is the most important Winter factor.’” Disney Enters., Inc. v.
                                  17   VidAngel, Inc., 869 F.3d 848, 856 (9th Cir. 2017) (quoting Garcia v. Google, Inc., 786
                                  18   F.3d 733, 740 (9th Cir. 2015)).
                                  19   II.     DISCUSSION
                                  20           The Court finds that all Winter factors have been met. Each factor is examined in
                                  21   turn.
                                  22           A.     Likelihood of Success on the Merits
                                  23           Just like the state court, this Court concludes that the NDA’s forum selection clause
                                  24   is valid and applicable to the ITC action. See State Ruling (dkt. 1-3) (“If Zync wishes to
                                  25   pursue this litigation, it must do so in Munich, Germany.”)
                                  26           “A forum selection clause is presumptively valid.” M/S Bremen v. Zapata Off-
                                  27   Shore Co., 407 U.S. 1, 15 (1972). A party challenging the clause bears a “heavy burden of
                                  28   proof” and must “clearly show that enforcement would be unreasonable and unjust, or that
                                                                                       2
                                            Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB       Document 53        Filed 06/22/26    Page 3 of 9




                                   1   the clause was invalid for such reasons as fraud or overreaching.” Id. As Zync’s counsel
                                   2   argued at the motion hearing, Zync’s main challenge to the validity of the clause is that the
                                   3   NDA is a contract of adhesion. See also Opp’n at 2. In her declaration, Rana Sobhany,
                                   4   Zync’s Chief Executive Officer, states that BMW “presented the NDA to Zync as a pre-
                                   5   signed, non-negotiable document.” Sobhany Decl. (dkt. 18) ¶ 13. But “take it or leave it”
                                   6   contracts “do not necessarily render a forum-selection clause unenforceable.” E. Bay
                                   7   Women’s Health, Inc. v. gloStream, Inc., 2014 WL 1618382, at *4 (N.D. Cal. Apr. 21,
                                   8   2014); see also Jocer Enters., Inc. v. Compass Constr., Inc., 2017 WL 4011134, at *3 (C.D.
                                   9   Cal. Sept. 12, 2017) (“[F]ederal law makes clear that even forum selection clauses
                                  10   included in contracts of adhesion are enforceable.”). Indeed, the state court agreed that the
                                  11   clause was valid and enforceable. See State Ruling. And Zync does not provide any
                                  12   compelling reason that the forum selection clause itself is unreasonable.
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           Moreover, the NDA covers the issues in the ITC action. The NDA explicitly
                                  14   applies “to all and any confidential information, including Trade Secrets, directly or
                                  15   indirectly disclosed by a Party or a Connected Company of a Party in connection with the
                                  16   Project.” NDA (dkt. 1-1) at 2. Zync’s ITC complaint plainly arises out of confidential
                                  17   information and trade secrets BMW purportedly stole for itself in violation of the NDA.
                                  18   See ITC Complaint (dkt. 1-6) ¶ 81 (“Unbeknownst to Zync at the time, while BMW was
                                  19   conveying optimism about the partnership, BMW was simultaneously preparing to
                                  20   distribute Zync’s proprietary materials to third parties.”). Zync attempts to escape the
                                  21   scope of the NDA by arguing that its ITC claims are independent from the NDA and do
                                  22   not require contract interpretation to reach the merits.1 See Sur-reply at 9–11. But Zync’s
                                  23   ITC complaint makes clear that its claims directly arise out of the parties’ rights under the
                                  24   PPA and the NDA. See ITC Complaint ¶ 66 (“BMW NA expressly agreed that it would
                                  25   not use Zync’s Platform or related information for any purpose beyond the pilot
                                  26
                                  27   1
                                         Zync asserts that both German and federal law requires narrow interpretations of forum selection
                                  28   clauses and that ambiguity must be resolved against the drafter. Sur-reply at 8. The Court agrees
                                       with that principle but does not find such ambiguity here.
                                                                                       3
                                            Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB       Document 53        Filed 06/22/26     Page 4 of 9




                                   1   evaluation.”); see also Kalbfus Decl. (dkt. 44-6) ¶ 10 (noting that German courts interpret
                                   2   forum selection clauses “as covering not only contractual claims but also concurring tort
                                   3   claims”). Moreover, when seeking a continuance for its anticipated motion to stay in state
                                   4   court, Zync admitted that the ITC action overlapped with the state case—which was
                                   5   dismissed based on the forum selection clause—and asserted “the same trade secret
                                   6   misappropriation allegations and nearly the same tortious interference allegations.” Dkt.
                                   7   10-4. Zync cannot represent that its ITC action is distinct before this Court when it argued
                                   8   the opposite before another.
                                   9           Zync raises two primary arguments against the forum selection clause: exception
                                  10   and waiver. See Opp’n at 6–7.
                                  11                  1.     Exception
                                  12           Zync points to the clause’s explicit exception for jurisdiction required by mandatory
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   law. NDA at 5. It argues that Section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1990 gives the ITC
                                  14   “exclusive authority to investigate unfair trade practices involving imported goods.”
                                  15   Opp’n at 7. But the law and Zync’s own conduct demonstrate that Section 337 does not
                                  16   require ITC jurisdiction.
                                  17           While the ITC is certainly a government entity empowered to investigate unfair
                                  18   import trade practices, it is by no means a mandatory forum. For starters, Section 337
                                  19   itself explains how the ITC does not have exclusive authority or jurisdiction, particularly in
                                  20   light of forum selection clauses. The ITC can, “on the basis of an agreement between the
                                  21   private parties to the investigation, including an agreement to present the matter for
                                  22   arbitration, terminate any [] investigation, in whole or in part.”2 19 U.S.C. § 1337(c). The
                                  23   ITC itself has recognized this statutory provision. See Certain Color Intraoral Scanners
                                  24   and Related Hardware & Software, No. 337-TA-1091, Order No. 23, at 10 (May 18, 2018)
                                  25   (Dkt. 10-5) at 4–5 (Cheney, Chief ALJ) (“The ‘agreement between the parties’ delineated
                                  26   in section 337(c) can be an agreement formed prior to the investigation . . . . A negotiated
                                  27
                                       2
                                  28     That the ITC is still considering BMW’s motion to terminate and earlier request to decline
                                       institution highlights the relevance of the statutory context for Zync’s argument.
                                                                                       4
                                            Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB       Document 53         Filed 06/22/26    Page 5 of 9




                                   1   forum selection clause . . . may inform the basis for terminating an investigation.”).
                                   2            It is also understood that “actions before [a] district court and the ITC can proceed
                                   3   in parallel.” Hoist Fitness Sys., Inc. v. TuffStuff Fitness Int’l, Inc., 2018 WL 8222261, at
                                   4   *1 (C.D. Cal. Dec. 20, 2018). Congress recognized this possibility when it permitted
                                   5   parties before the ITC to request a stay of parallel court proceedings. See 28 U.S.C.
                                   6   § 1659(a) (permitting a request for a stay 30 days after a party is named a respondent
                                   7   before the ITC or 30 days after a district court action is filed). Moreover, the Federal
                                   8   Circuit has recognized that the ITC does not have exclusive jurisdiction when it affirmed
                                   9   an injunction requiring a party to withdraw an ITC complaint in light of a forum selection
                                  10   clause.3 Gen. Protecht Grp., Inc. v. Leviton Mfg. Co., 651 F.3d 1355, 1366 (Fed. Cir.
                                  11   2011).
                                  12            Further, Zync’s conduct in this case demonstrates its understanding that ITC
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   jurisdiction is not required. Zync itself first filed in state court, rather than before the ITC.
                                  14   And when seeking a continuance based on its intended motion to stay, Zync never brought
                                  15   up its argument that Section 337 mandated jurisdiction before the ITC.
                                  16            Zync makes additional, unpersuasive arguments. Zync points to its German law
                                  17   expert, Dr. Bernhard Arnold, who concluded that “Section 337 falls within [the NDA’s]
                                  18   mandatory-law carveout.” Sur-reply at 6. But Dr. Arnold offered his opinion assuming
                                  19   “that the ITC rejects attempts to challenge its competence based solely on forum choice.”
                                  20   Arnold Decl. (dkt. 40-1) ¶ 26. As discussed, Section 337 does permit the ITC to terminate
                                  21   investigations solely based on forum selection clauses.
                                  22            Zync also focuses on the types of relief available. Notwithstanding the fact that
                                  23   available relief has nothing to do with whether jurisdiction is required, the Court addresses
                                  24   these points. Zync argues that “[o]nly the ITC can investigate Section 337 unfair
                                  25   importation claims and issue an exclusion order directed to unfairly traded imports at the
                                  26
                                       3
                                  27     Zync attempts to distinguish General Protecht by pointing out that it “did not involve a
                                       mandatory-law carveout.” Sur-reply at 8. But that misses the point. If the ITC truly had
                                  28   exclusive, required jurisdiction, it would not matter that there was no mandatory law exception in
                                       the forum selection clause at-issue.
                                                                                        5
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB         Document 53        Filed 06/22/26    Page 6 of 9




                                   1   U.S. border.” Sur-reply at 6. That is incorrect. While it is true that “the ITC can issue
                                   2   exclusion orders,” it is also true that courts have “the authority to issue the same forms of
                                   3   relief as the ITC.” Freres v. Yucheng Lujian Biological Co., 2009 WL 3135175, at *2
                                   4   (D.N.J. Sept. 25, 2009). Additionally, Zync asserts that German courts “cannot replicate
                                   5   Section 337’s sovereign border remedy.” Sur-reply at 7. But as BMW points out, German
                                   6   courts can grant injunctive relief for trade secret claims. See Reply at 5 (discussing
                                   7   Section 6 of the Trade Secrets Protection Act (GeschGehG)); see also Arnold Decl. ¶ 35
                                   8   (same). Moreover, Zync could potentially have a district court recognize a German
                                   9   judgment and then “take the additional step of requesting the U.S. Customs Service to
                                  10   enforce the district court judgment by seizing the offending goods.” See Texas
                                  11   Instruments Inc. v. Tessera, Inc., 231 F.3d 1325, 1330 (Fed. Cir. 2000) (noting that ITC
                                  12   enforcement is faster but that a plaintiff can still obtain exclusionary relief through courts).
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13          Accordingly, the Court is not persuaded by Zync’s argument.
                                  14                 2.     Waiver
                                  15          Zync also makes arguments related to BMW’s purported waiver by filing in this
                                  16   Court, rather than Germany.
                                  17          First, Zync asserts that BMW waived its rights under the forum selection clause by
                                  18   litigating in the ITC and then filing this action. Not so. “Courts find waiver only where a
                                  19   party has taken actions inconsistent with [a forum selection clause], or delayed its
                                  20   enforcement, and enforcement would prejudice other parties.” Google LLC v. NAO
                                  21   Tsargrad Media, 2025 WL 964692, at *9 (N.D. Cal. Mar. 31, 2025) (citation modified),
                                  22   appeal dismissed, 2025 WL 4704152 (9th Cir. Dec. 17, 2025). That is not the case here.
                                  23   To the contrary, BMW (and BMW NA) has consistently acted to enforce the clause.
                                  24   BMW sought dismissal based on the forum selection clause both before the state court and
                                  25   the ITC—forums where Zync filed claims. See Opp’n at 4. The state court agreed with
                                  26   BMW and the ITC declined to reach the merits at that stage. Id. Even before this Court,
                                  27   BMW seeks to enforce the parties’ forum selection clause. See Compl; cf. Applied Med.
                                  28   Distribution Corp. v. Surgical Co. BV, 587 F.3d 909, 919 (9th Cir. 2009) (“Anti-suit
                                                                                      6
                                            Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB       Document 53         Filed 06/22/26    Page 7 of 9




                                   1   injunctions may be the only viable way to effectuate valid forum selection clauses.”). That
                                   2   is not conduct establishing a waiver.
                                   3           Without citation to legal authority, Zync argues that BMW’s requested relief is fatal
                                   4   because a Munich court cannot enjoin parties before the ITC. Sur-reply at 11. The Court
                                   5   does not see how that is relevant to the enforceability of the forum selection clause at
                                   6   issue, particularly where Zync has now filed in two separate forums (and lost in one) that
                                   7   are not in Munich.
                                   8           Consequently, the Court finds that BMW has established a likelihood of success on
                                   9   the merits.4
                                  10           B.     Irreparable Harm
                                  11           “Courts around the country regularly hold that the ‘depriv[ation] of [a] bargained-
                                  12   for choice of forum’ constitutes irreparable harm sufficient to support an injunction.”
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   Google, 2025 WL 964692 at *11 (quoting Nippon Shinyaku Co. v. Sarepta Therapeutics,
                                  14   Inc., 25 F.4th 998, 1008 (Fed. Cir. 2022)); Interdigital Tech. Corp. v. Pegatron Corp., 2015
                                  15   WL 3958257, at *9 (N.D. Cal. June 29, 2015) (same). And “an ITC proceeding can have a
                                  16   direct and significant impact on a responding party.” General Protecht Group, 651 F.3d at
                                  17   1364 (emphasis in original) (affirming finding of irreparable harm by litigating before the
                                  18   ITC and other courts despite a forum selection clause).
                                  19           But Zync is correct that BMW’s delay cuts against it. As Zync notes, BMW did not
                                  20   seek relief before this Court until after the state court found in its favor, even though it
                                  21   plainly knew about its forum selection clause from the very start. See Sur-reply at 14.
                                  22   That being said, BMW’s delay was not so substantial as conduct in other cases where
                                  23   parties waived their rights to forum selection clauses. See Media Matters for Am. v. X
                                  24   Corp., 2025 WL 3688854, at *2 (9th Cir. Dec. 19, 2025) (active litigation for over a year
                                  25
                                  26   4
                                        Zync also challenges BMW’s motion by asserting that mandatory injunctive relief would not
                                  27   preserve the status quo, as pausing an investigation dismantles the status quo, rather than
                                       preserving it. Opp’n at 5. But anti-suit injunctions based on valid forum selection clauses are
                                  28   considered proper because “there is an absence of a legal remedy” without them. Interdigital
                                       Tech. Corp. v. Pegatron Corp., 2015 WL 3958257, at *9 (N.D. Cal. June 29, 2015).
                                                                                        7
                                            Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB      Document 53        Filed 06/22/26    Page 8 of 9




                                   1   before invoking forum selection clause).
                                   2           Accordingly, the Court finds that BMW has shown irreparable harm.
                                   3           C.    Balance of the Equities
                                   4           The balance of the equities tips in BMW’s favor. As discussed, BMW would face
                                   5   hardship by being deprived of its forum selection clause and litigating in multiple forums.
                                   6   Moreover, “[h]aving contracted for a specific forum, [Zync] should not be heard to argue
                                   7   that the enforcement of the contract into which it freely entered would cause hardship.”
                                   8   General Protecht Group, 651 F.3d at 1365. And Zync has not demonstrated that it would
                                   9   be unable to get substantially similar relief from an action in Munich.
                                  10           D.    Public Interest
                                  11           The public interest factor also weighs in BMW’s favor. “Public policy strongly
                                  12   favors the enforcement of forum selection clauses.” Koken v. Stateco Inc., 2006 WL
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   2918050, at *8 (N.D. Cal. Oct. 11, 2006). While Zync is correct that the public has an
                                  14   interest in the ITC’s protection, it does not change the calculus here. See Sur-reply at 17–
                                  15   18. As discussed, courts can just as easily address the goals of the ITC—that is why there
                                  16   are parallel cases and why courts have enjoined parties from engaging in ITC actions
                                  17   before. Indeed, Section 337 itself recognizes the policy in favor of forum selection clauses
                                  18   as it explicitly permits termination of investigations based only on forum selection clauses.
                                  19   See 19 U.S.C. § 1337(c).
                                  20   III.    CONCLUSION
                                  21           For the foregoing reasons, the Court GRANTS BMW’s motion for a preliminary
                                  22   injunction. Zync must request a stay of the ITC proceedings until the state court appeal is
                                  23   resolved, when the state judgement becomes final if affirmed.5
                                  24           Additionally, BMW is ordered to pay a bond of $10,000 pursuant to Federal Rule of
                                  25
                                       5
                                  26     Zync asserts that BMW NA is an indispensable party and that BMW did not include BMW NA
                                       as a party because it “would destroy diversity jurisdiction.” See Sur-reply at 12 n.4. But that
                                  27   would exclude BMW NA as a required party under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 19, as joinder
                                       would deprive the Court of subject-matter jurisdiction. See Fed. R. Civ. P. 19(a). Nevertheless,
                                  28   the Court’s injunction binds Zync, which is a party before the Court. See Fed. R. Civ. P.
                                       65(d)(2)(A).
                                                                                      8
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB      Document 53       Filed 06/22/26   Page 9 of 9




                                   1   Civil Procedure 65(c).
                                   2         IT IS SO ORDERED.
